x: Many good things came out of the swinging sixties and not least of them is the subject of this edition's "Spotlight" - Simon Shirley. Born in Nottingham on 3rd August 1966, Simon spent the first seven years of his life in the UK before his family emigrated to New Zealand.

Meanwhile, newly eligible decathlete Simon Shirley was holding on to third spot in the long jump and quickly switched to the 'B' 100 as two-thirds of our sprint squad had not appeared.

Roger Te Puni, Simon Shirley and Fred Salle were other competitors while Jon Ridgeon and John Regis were prominent among the sporting elite who attended to pay their last respects to a man who has done so much for our sport over the last 30 years.
John Regis (1) takes the back stretch, passing the baton on to Simon Shirley (2) at New River Stadium during B.A.L. match 4.

Others for the masochist stakes were: Simon Shirley - gaining second in both the 'B' long jump and the 'B' javelin plus the sprint relay, Lennie Paul - sprints and relay, Paul Beaumont - 400 hurdles, 400 flat and long relay.
What a boon it is to have an international class decathlete in the team; Simon Shirley takes on the mantle of "B" javelin thrower at New River [b].
Our multi-eventer Simon Shirley has also been in action over the winter, competing in sprints, hurdles, throws and jumps in the Gatorade meetings.

Together with regulars Gary McKernan and Mike Small, Abi Ekoku, Warren Caswell and Simon Shirley wreaked havoc on the field, pushed us to a match winning situation and had the unhappy Ilford team manager requesting the previous BAL team sheet to check that we weren't pulling a fast one.
Simon Shirley, making a welcome return, won the 'B' long jump while Dennis Costello looked a different man as he had a marginally windy 7.39m to finish 4th in the 'A' string.

Representing Britain as one of a four man team, Simon Shirley had the misfortune to pick up an injury in the long jump and was unable to finish the first day's events. 100m/11.6, LJ/6.92, SP/12.33, HJ:/1.92.
Two years ago Simon Shirley presented a sorry sight.
